title: Museum of Innocence
author: Orhan Pamuk
notes: This book made me reflect on my feelings and my understanding of love. Love can be something so fragile while also being something so powerful; love is for two, and at the same time, love can be kept alive only in one’s own mind. It describes so neatly how yearning changes one’s perception of the surroundings. It makes one deeply feel through words how innocent of a feeling love is. This novel forces you to read not only with eyes and brain, but with mind and heart.

title: Dom Casmurro
author: Machado de Assis
notes: Dom Casmurro is the memoir of a man who felt deeply in love to Capitu. He did everything that he could to finally marry her. Latter In life, he starts to think if his wife betrayed him or not with his best friend. This book has divided readers for more than one century into two groups based on this question: Did Capitu cheat? The author left us without answers, so depends on the reader to make its own opinions. This book invites you to see how love can change lives.

title: Chander and Sudha
author: Dharamvir Bharati
notes: The book explores what love is through the relationship between Sudha and Chander, and other characters that are part of their life. It shows the complexities of love, desire, morality, devotion and sacrifice. As the story progresses, it is fascinating to see how Sudha's and Chander's understanding of love changes. This makes them question whether idealizing love sometimes prevents us from accepting it in its natural, imperfect form. I would also recommend this book for its thoughtful exploration of marriage and its relationship with love. The story leaves us with uncomfortable realities of relationship, love, morality and how our own ideals shape the choices we make in the name of love.
